title: Credit-spread sleeve hedge
hypothesis: The live book keeps the 3x sleeve on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is the weakness in the refreshed subperiod table: the trend-core book trails SPY in 2020 and again in 2022. A widening credit spread is a faster stress signal. When the 20-session change in the spread exceeds a precommitted threshold, move only the leveraged sleeve to T-bills. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The sleeve goes back to UPRO when the trend is on and the 20-session widening is back at or below the threshold.

title: Trailing-peak stop on the UPRO sleeve
hypothesis: The live sleeve stays on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is why the trend-core drawdown is still about -46.8%, and why the book trailed SPY in 2020 and 2022. The 2026-10-26 volatility scale cut the sleeve whenever realized volatility was high, including in high-vol rallies, and gained 2.6 drawdown points, short of 3, with a negative improvement Sharpe. The 2026-10-27 multi-lookback vote was never selected, so the stitched path matched the current book, and the vote cells themselves had deeper drawdowns. A trailing-peak stop cuts only the UPRO sleeve after SPY has already fallen from its own high, so a high-vol rally that is still near that high stays invested. title: N-day confirmation of the 200-day band
hypothesis: The live sleeve already uses a 2% hysteresis band: it turns on only when SPY closes above 1.02 times its 200-day average and turns off only when the close is below 0.98 times that average. That rule, and a 0% band, are already in the original grid. A single close through the band still flips the sleeve, and the new state then sticks until the other side of the band. Those one-session pierces are the whipsaw: the book pays the 5 bp UPRO cost and the leveraged overnight gap, then often sits in the new state through a reversal. This test does not rescore the 2% band by itself. It requires N consecutive closes beyond the band before the state changes. A close that is not beyond the band in the flip direction resets the count, and the previous state is kept until the count is met. Bands are 0.5%, 1%, 2%, and 3%. Confirmation counts are 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 sessions. The cell with a 2% band and 1 day is the live filter, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep the current book. Every other cell is a new trial. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

title: Off-trend core hold in T-bills
hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. The credit-spread hedge, the volatility scale, the multi-lookback vote, the trailing-peak stop, and the N-day band confirmation all tried to get the UPRO sleeve out of equities sooner. They left that trough in place: by the time the drawdown bottoms, the sleeve is already in T-bills and the loss that remains is the SPY half, which the 200-day band never turns off. The idle-diversifier test then moved that residual equity into GLD, IEF, or TLT. It was rejected, and those assets made the stitched drawdown worse. This test does not buy another risky asset and does not change the sleeve's entry rule. While the same 200-day 2% band is off, only a fraction of the core budget stays in SPY (or in SSO when the three-down-close dip is on). The rest of that budget earns T-bills, the same cash the sleeve already earns. Fractions are 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1. The fraction 1 is the live book, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep the current book. While the band is on, the book is the unchanged 50/50 trend core, including the dip on the core. A trend flip resizes only the invested share of the core pile and moves the sleeve; it does not reset drifted pile sizes. The quarterly mix still resets both piles. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

title: Yield-curve recession clock
hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. Sleeve-exit rules (the credit-spread hedge, the volatility scale, the multi-lookback vote, the trailing-peak stop, and the N-day band confirmation) left that trough in place, because by then the UPRO sleeve is already in T-bills and the loss that remains is the SPY half. Parking part of that half in T-bills whenever the 200-day band is off did cut the drawdown, and it was rejected: the cash stake ran through every off-trend episode, including the rebounds that are not recessions, and the CAGR give-up was larger than the bar allows. This test does not key off the equity trend. The trigger is the Treasury curve. The spread is the 10-year yield minus the 13-week bill yield, both in percent as Yahoo quotes ^TNX and ^IRX. Equity damage after an inversion has historically arrived as the curve later re-steepens, so the rule is not cash while the spread is negative. A session starts the clock when the spread crosses from at or above a depth to strictly below it. From that close, for a fixed number of sessions including that close, the whole book, core and sleeve and the three-down-close dip, earns T-bills. A crossing while the clock is already running does not extend it. After the clock the book returns to the unchanged 50/50 trend core, including the dip. title: Sized trend-gated dip
hypothesis: The live overlay swaps the entire SPY half into 2x SSO after three strictly down closes, then leaves at the first up close or five sessions. It does that whether or not the 200-day band is on. The study's recorded full-sample table already shows the cost of that choice: the 50/50 book without the overlay has Sharpe 0.53 and max drawdown -46.1% with turnover 0.8 a year, and the same book with the overlay has Sharpe 0.52 and max drawdown -46.8% with turnover 13.6. The later iterations tried to repair the -46.8% trough on 2009-03-09 by removing equity: a faster UPRO exit, cash in place of the core whenever the band is off, or cash for the whole book after a curve inversion. Those cuts reached the trough by selling the SPY half, and the rebound they sat out made the improvement's Sharpe fail the deflated-Sharpe cutoff and pushed the CAGR give-up past half a point. This test does not sell the core and does not change the sleeve's entry. It changes the overlay that adds leverage on down closes. A new dip starts only when the 200-day 2% band is on at that close. If the band turns off while a dip is held, the dip flattens at that close and does not re-enter until a fresh three-down signal with the band on. The first-up exit and the five-session cap stay. The original protocol already scored five entry rules at a full SSO swap; this grid does not rescore those entries. While a dip is on, only a fixed fraction of the core pile is SSO and the rest stays SPY. Fractions are 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1. Gates are ungated and trend-on. The ungated fraction 1 is the live book, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep the current book. The other seven cells are new trials. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

title: One-sided UPRO drift band
hypothesis: The live book resets both piles to 50/50 on a quarterly calendar. Between those dates the sleeve is 3x while the trend is on, so a rally lifts its weight above one half and the book carries the extra leverage until the calendar date. That same date also trades when the drift is small, and it buys the sleeve back after the sleeve has shrunk. The original grid compared monthly and quarterly calendars. It did not test a no-trade band. Earlier iterations tried to cut the -46.8% trough by selling the SPY half, by parking the whole book in T-bills after a curve inversion, or by getting UPRO out on a faster signal. Those rules were rejected. The sized dip changed the overlay and was rejected too. This test does not add a regime signal and does not sell the core. It replaces the quarterly mix date. After the close, if the sleeve is in UPRO and its weight is strictly above one half by more than a fixed band, the next open resets both piles to 50/50. If the weight is at or below that ceiling, or the sleeve is in T-bills, the piles are left alone, including when UPRO has fallen below half. A trend flip still swaps the sleeve instrument and does not by itself resize the piles. The three-down-close dip is unchanged. Bands are 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 percentage points, fixed before this sample is scored. The quarterly calendar is the current book, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep it. The five bands are new trials. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

title: Fast re-entry of the SPY core
hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. Faster exits of the UPRO sleeve left that trough in place. Parking the SPY half in T-bills for the entire time the 200-day band is off did cut the drawdown by more than 3 points, and it was rejected because the cash stake also sat out the rebound and the CAGR give-up was larger than half a point. Replacing that cash with bonds or gold, and parking the whole book after a curve inversion, failed for the same reason: the rebound that was missed cost more CAGR than the bar allows. The one-sided drift band and the sized dip did not touch that trough. This test does not change the sleeve's 200-day rule and does not hold a constant cash fraction for the whole off-trend episode. While the 200-day 2% band is on, the book is the unchanged trend core. While that band is off, the core is in SPY, or in SSO when the three-down-close dip is on, only when a shorter trend filter is on, and in T-bills when that shorter filter is off. The sleeve stays in T-bills until the 200-day band turns back on. The shorter filter uses the same hysteresis as the live band: it turns on only above the average times one plus the band and off only below the average times one minus the band. Windows are 20, 50, and 100 sessions. Bands are 0 and 2%. The six cells are new trials. The current book, which never moves the core to T-bills, is the walk-forward's option to keep the present rule and is not a new trial. A constant off-trend cash fraction is not in this grid. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.
